all-of-grace: All of Grace is Charles Spurgeon’s plain and earnest presentation of the gospel, written for the reader who longs to be saved but does not know where to begin. Step by step he shows that God justifies the ungodly, that salvation is by grace through faith and not by works, and that repentance and faith are themselves God’s gifts. Warm, direct, and rich in homely illustration, it presses one invitation: come to Christ just as you are.
answers-to-prayer: George Müller, who cared for thousands of orphans in Bristol without asking anyone but God for support, here records specific answers to prayer drawn from his own narratives. From the beginning of the orphan work to the great houses on Ashley Down, he shows how need after need was met in response to believing prayer. A quiet, factual testimony that God still hears and provides.
around-the-wicket-gate: Charles Spurgeon wrote this little book for those who linger just outside the gate of salvation—awakened, anxious, almost persuaded, yet not believing. With characteristic warmth and urgency he clears away the difficulties that keep seekers from Christ, showing how simple faith really is and why nothing short of it will do. A friendly hand stretched out to any reader who is near the kingdom but not yet in it.
cheque-book: In this beloved daily devotional, Charles Spurgeon treats each promise of Scripture as a cheque drawn on the Bank of Faith—to be endorsed by personal faith and presented to God for fulfilment. Written, as his preface tells, in a time of deep personal trial, these readings for every day of the year are brief, rich, and full of comfort for believers in need.
days-of-heaven-upon-earth: A daily devotional from A. B. Simpson, offering a short Scripture text and meditation for every day of the year. These readings call believers to walk in the fullness of Christ moment by moment, so that ordinary days become days of heaven upon earth.
life-and-diary-of-david-brainerd: The life and diary of David Brainerd, the young missionary to the American Indians in the 1740s, prepared for publication by Jonathan Edwards. Its pages trace his conversion, his labours and hardships in the wilderness, and above all his extraordinary life of prayer and longing after God. It has stirred generations of readers to deeper devotion and missionary sacrifice.
prevailing-prayer: D. L. Moody examines what makes prayer prevail with God, walking through its great elements one by one: adoration, confession, restitution, thanksgiving, forgiveness, unity, faith, petition, and submission. Illustrated throughout with the prayers of the Bible and with striking answers to prayer, it is a practical call to earnest, expectant praying.
revival-lectures: Charles Finney’s famous lectures on the nature of revival—what a revival of religion is, when it may be expected, and how it may be promoted. He deals searchingly with prevailing prayer, the spirit of prayer, being filled with the Spirit, and the means God uses to awaken sinners and revive His church. Plain-spoken and demanding, these lectures have influenced generations of Christians.
susanna-wesley-clarke: Eliza Clarke’s biography of Susanna Wesley, mother of John and Charles Wesley, whose ordered household and patient teaching at Epworth helped shape two of the great figures of English Christianity. It follows her from birth to widowhood—her marriage, her method of training her children, the rectory fire, and the trials and steadfast faith of her later years. A portrait of quiet, persevering godliness in the midst of hardship.
the-fourfold-gospel: A. B. Simpson’s classic statement of the fourfold gospel: Christ our Saviour, Christ our Sanctifier, Christ our Healer, and Christ our Coming Lord. In these brief chapters Simpson presents a whole Christ for the whole person, calling believers beyond forgiveness into sanctification, healing, and the blessed hope of His return.
the-gospel-of-healing: A. B. Simpson sets out the scriptural foundation for divine healing, answers popular objections, and gives practical directions to those who would trust Christ as Healer. The book closes with testimony, including Simpson’s own account of the healing that transformed his life and ministry.
the-way-to-god: D. L. Moody’s simple, earnest presentation of the way of salvation. Beginning with the love of God that passes knowledge, he leads the reader through the gateway of the new birth, repentance, and the assurance of salvation, with words of counsel for young believers and a warning against backsliding. Direct and unadorned, it presses one question: have you entered in?
things-as-they-are: Amy Carmichael’s unvarnished account of missionary work in southern India—written to show things as they are, not as friends at home might wish them to be. In vivid scenes from village life she describes the grip of caste and idolatry and the real cost of winning even one soul. A sobering, honest book, and a moving call to prayer for those still unreached.
till-he-come: A collection of Charles Spurgeon’s communion meditations and addresses, prepared to help believers at the Lord’s Table remember their Master “till He come.” Spurgeon dwells on the nearness of Christ, the sweetness of His love, and the rest of redeemed souls freed from fear. Devotional reading of the richest kind for any who would draw near to their Lord.
union-and-communion: Hudson Taylor’s meditations on the Song of Solomon, tracing the soul’s progress from first communion with Christ into deep and unbroken union with Him. Written by the founder of the China Inland Mission, it is a brief but searching guide to intimacy with the Lord.
way-into-holiest: F. B. Meyer’s devotional exposition of the Epistle to the Hebrews, tracing its great theme: the way into the holiest opened by the blood of Jesus. Chapter by chapter Meyer unfolds the dignity and priesthood of Christ, the peril of drifting and unbelief, and the rest of faith, applying the epistle’s message with his characteristic warmth and practical insight.
